title: First confirmed ascent
summary: On 29 May 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit. This marks the end of the early exploratory era, not the cause of the much later rise in success.
prompt: Use the comparison to separate the milestone from the longer trend. One successful expedition says nothing about what a typical later expedition achieved.

label: 1990s
title: Commercial expeditions expand
summary: Commercial Himalayan mountaineering expanded from around 1990. Professional guiding changed who could attempt an expedition and how logistical support was organised.
prompt: Compare hired support and oxygen with success. These changes overlap in time, but this view cannot separate the effects of guiding, equipment, forecasting and accumulated route knowledge.

source.label: Westhoff et al. · commercialisation and survival

title: Avalanche and South-side cancellation
summary: An avalanche killed 16 Sherpa guides and the Nepal-side season was subsequently cancelled. The database's expedition notes record the avalanche, strike and abandoned attempts.
prompt: Look for Season closure in How expeditions ended. Many members stopped before oxygen would have been used, so a no-oxygen record here is not a fair test of climbing without oxygen.
dataNote: Closure classification comes from the dataset's termnote field; the news source supplies historical context.

title: Earthquake and avalanche
summary: The Nepal earthquake triggered an avalanche at Everest Base Camp and the season was abandoned. It is a separate event from the 2014 avalanche and strike.
prompt: Compare the closure share with surrounding periods. Then remember this event when Your plan explains why cancelled 2014–15 expeditions are excluded from model fitting.
dataNote: Closure classification comes from the dataset's termnote field; the news source supplies historical context.

title: COVID-19 permit suspension
summary: Nepal and China suspended spring climbing permits during the COVID-19 pandemic. Only three Everest expeditions remain in this historical snapshot for 2020.
prompt: Treat the event year as an interruption with a very small sample, not as evidence that climbing became less safe or that later success was caused by the pandemic.

source.label: ABC News · Nepal and China suspend permits
